quote: the electric company went crazy. They sent me a $2,300.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a huge, specific bill figure completely unprompted — this is the single richest anchor in the call — and the rep's next line ignores it entirely to ask about tree removal instead.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have deliberately let it pass to keep focus on the roof/photo logistics needed to build the design at all. This is weaker than the reactive read because the rep never returns to the number even after logistics are settled.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect big bill numbers back immediately — even a simple 'wow, $2,300, that's exactly why people book with us' — to convert disclosed pain into forward momentum before returning to logistics.

quote: I've got two trees that can handle the, hail. And I'm not trying to I'll take these both of them down.
stewart_read: Customer volunteering to remove more trees for solar viability is a strong buying signal — he is actively solving the rep's stated design obstacle unprompted.
coaching_implication: Rep should have explicitly named this as removing the blocker to booking: 'once those two come down, there's nothing standing between you and a great design' — reinforcing urgency toward a locked appointment.

quote: I'll send you a quick text to if you wouldn't wouldn't mind if you have time later today to send me a photo just of kind of the back of your roof.
stewart_read: This is the moment the rep should be running verify + booking a hard appointment, but instead the entire remainder of the call becomes about collecting a photo via text with no date/time ever set.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep felt genuinely blocked without a clear roof view and needed the photo before designing. Strategic case is weak — nothing prevented the rep from booking a specific day/time appointment now and having the photo sent before then.
coaching_implication: Coach: photo collection and appointment booking are not mutually exclusive. Book the day/time first, then request the photo as a pre-appointment task.

quote: just send me a photo when you can. We'll start on our end, and then we can kinda figure out a time over text. Would that work for you?
stewart_read: The call's actual close has no day, no time, no hour-block statement, and no verbal handshake beyond a vague 'would that work for you' — this is a textbook procedural soft-exit on a customer who was ready to book from minute one.
coaching_implication: This is the coaching centerpiece: an eager customer was let leave the call without a single locked detail. Replay this clip — the rep had every opening to say 'let's get you on the calendar for Thursday at 2' and never did.

quote: hoping y'all come and put it in.
stewart_read: Customer opens the call already wanting the install — about as strong an interest signal as a setter will get — yet the rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar' or validates/expands on this enthusiasm.
coaching_implication: Even with an already-sold customer, the rep should confirm and amplify the motivation stated, then use it to justify locking the appointment immediately rather than letting the conversation wander.

quote: I'm okay with, putting it out in my yard or putting a carport or a building out in front and, putting it on top of that. However.
stewart_read: Customer is openly floating a ground-mount or new structure (carport/building) as an alternative to roof mounting — this is adjacent to Ion's cross-sell scenarios and at minimum needs specialist framing, but the rep does not acknowledge or route it.
alternative_hypothesis: This may not map cleanly to the roofing cross-sell trigger since it's a new structure, not a roof replacement — but it's still unaddressed customer-initiated content the rep should not have silently passed over.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to flag non-standard mounting scenarios (ground mount, new structure) explicitly for the closer/design team rather than letting it pass unacknowledged.

stewart_read: Customer signals fatigue at the close of a rambling, unstructured call; rep does not acknowledge this at all and moves straight to a scripted goodbye.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be interpreted as casual small talk rather than a vulnerability disclosure, which is why it is not weighted as heavily as a true vulnerability moment — but it still reflects the call's drifting shape.
coaching_implication: Minor, but worth naming: a tighter, more structured call would likely not have left the customer sounding worn out at the end.
